definition: Rectitude means moral uprightness; strict honesty in one's dealings.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rectitude. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rectitude should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Everyone trusted the scorekeeper's rectitude: she once erased her own daughter's point total and re-added it in front of witnesses.
Honesty is a much milder claim than rectitude — the truth told when asked, the change counted right — while rectitude means a whole career of dealings held straight, rule by rule.
Saintliness goes further than rectitude — it gives away the coat no rule required; rectitude keeps every rule to the letter, asked or not.

Integrity is wholeness of character — the broad, warm, everyday word for a person whose actions match their values. Rectitude is sterner and more formal: strict, auditable straightness in one's dealings, every rule kept whether or not anyone is watching or asking.

Uprightness is the same straightness of conduct said plainly — the ordinary word for someone who deals fair and keeps their hands clean. Rectitude is its formal, slightly starched register, the term a citation or a court opinion reaches for, carrying an extra shade of strictness.

When the province needed someone to run its new lottery, it passed over livelier candidates for Odile Marchand, a retired bank examiner.
Her rectitude was already a byword: in thirty years of audits she had never accepted so much as a cup of coffee from a bank under review.
She brought the same strictness to the lottery office -- every drawing filmed, every rule published, her own tickets forbidden by a rule she wrote herself.
Critics called the regime cold.
Marchand agreed, cheerfully.
Warmth, she said, could be counterfeited; a record in which every rule is kept to the letter, watched or unwatched, cannot.
